comparator.name: Politics, Psychology, Law and Economics
comparator.academicYear: Current UvA PPLE curriculum structure, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme structure totals 180 EC: a 102-EC compulsory shared interdisciplinary core, 66 EC in the selected specialisation together with the Bachelor’s thesis, and 12 EC of electives. The generic target offers Politics, Psychology, Law and Economics specialisations. None is identified as the broad default; Politics is first in the official programme name and curriculum order and is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break before UCR course selection. The official source publishes the shared core and major/thesis as formal aggregate credit buckets, which are preserved rather than subdivided without evidence.

components.name: Compulsory interdisciplinary core curriculum: eight interdisciplinary courses, four integrative seminars and four methodological courses
components.note: The current official programme structure reports this compulsory shared core as 102 EC.

components.name: Politics specialisation and Bachelor's thesis
components.note: The current official structure reports specialisation courses and the thesis together as 66 EC; Politics is selected using the neutral official-order tie-break.

components.name: Electives based on personal interests
components.note: Genuine elective space is preserved without inventing particular courses.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has sustained political, psychological, legal and economic strands rather than allowing any one field to stand for the whole programme.

alternatives.concept: Organises the four fields around behavioural public policy: psychology and behavioural economics explain decision-making, while politics, law, data and public economics examine how institutions design and evaluate interventions.

alternatives.labelRationale: The curriculum’s centre of gravity is behavioural and economic explanation of public decisions, supported by political institutions, law and quantitative analysis.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad four-field plan, this route gives substantially more weight to psychology, behavioural economics, data and policy evaluation and less to international history and global governance. More than four courses differ, and the organising question shifts to how behaviour and incentives shape public intervention.

alternatives.concept: Organises the four fields around justice and governance, combining public, international, constitutional and private law with politics, economics, social psychology and negotiation to examine how institutions allocate rights, power and resources.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: This route replaces much of the international-governance and data emphasis of the closest plan and the behavioural-policy emphasis of the second plan with a sustained public, private, constitutional, European and international law sequence. It differs from each earlier curriculum by more than 30 EC.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic bachelor requires one of four equally presented disciplinary specialisations and identifies no broad default. Politics appears first in the official programme name and curriculum order, so it is selected neutrally before and independently of UCR course selection.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first plan is the closest integrated response to PPLE across its four named disciplines. The behavioural-public-policy and law/justice/economic-governance directions are separately supported by direct and stable programme interests, produce coherent curricula and pass the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor. Production therefore stops at the maximum of three.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: The official 66-EC bucket combines the selected Politics specialisation with the thesis; it cannot be aligned one-to-one with a single 7.5-EC UCR course.
The official 102-EC shared core integrates sixteen compulsory courses across four fields and methods; no single UCR course reproduces this aggregate component.
The comparator preserves 12 EC of genuine elective space, which has no fixed subject counterpart in the selected UCR curricula.

comparator.note: The current official structure reports specialisation courses and the thesis together as 66 EC; Politics is selected using the neutral official-order tie-break.

notes.text: PPLE has a compulsory 102-EC interdisciplinary core followed by one formal disciplinary specialisation and a Bachelor’s thesis. UCR can combine substantial politics, psychology, law, economics and methods study, but it does not reproduce PPLE’s integrated course sequence, small-cohort seminars or formal major structure.
